passages.incorrect: In many cities, governments must decide whether budgets should be used to expand roads or to improve buses, trains and public services. Supporters of road construction argue that vehicles remain essential for families, businesses and emergency services, in areas where transport is infrequent. Although new roads can shorten particular journeys, but their wider effects are more complicated. This essay will discuss both positions and explain why I believe that investment should favour public transport while road improvements are necessary. Those who favour roads point out that buses cannot reach every home, factory or rural community. People is also more willing to travel at a convenient time when they can drive directly from one place to another. In addition, much delivery vehicles need routes so that shops, hospitals and construction sites can receive goods without delays. Widening a dangerous junction or repairing an ageing bridge may therefore contribute to reduce accidents and support the local economy. Road projects can be completed, which may make them easier for towns to finance. These arguments are persuasive when existing roads are unsafe or when communities have no alternative to driving. On the other hands, continually adding road space often encourages additional car use instead of solving congestion permanently. When driving becomes easier, some residents move farther from work, and others abandon buses that previously seemed acceptable. As a result, a new road may fill with traffic within a few years, while the city must pay for maintenance, policing and parking. By contrast, frequent and affordable public transport can move much passengers through crowded districts using far less space. It can prevent commuters to depend on cars for every journey and can give older people, teenagers and low-income workers independence. People has more confidence in a transport network when services arrive on time, stations feel safe and fares are clear. Investment in electric buses and railways can also contribute to improve air quality, particularly along busy urban corridors. Although public transport requires large initial spending, but its benefits are shared by a broader section of society. Critics correctly note that an empty bus or train is wasteful, and poorly planned routes can prevent residents to reach jobs efficiently. On the other hands, this weakness is mainly an argument for better planning rather than for abandoning public transport. Authorities should study travel patterns, coordinate timetables and provide smaller feeder buses in less densely populated neighbourhoods. They should also maintain roads that carry buses, ambulances and commercial traffic, because public and private transport depend on some of the same infrastructure. In my view, the strongest policy is not to choose one system absolutely, but to give public transport priority and reserve road spending for safety, maintenance and genuine access gaps. A dependable network of buses and trains offers a long-term response to congestion, inequality and pollution, whereas indiscriminate road expansion risks creating more demand. Therefore, governments should first make shared transport attractive enough to become the normal choice, while ensuring that essential roads remain safe and functional.

ruleFamilies.name: Use a gerund after selected prepositional to in contribute to, while excluding nominal and purpose frames
ruleFamilies.explanationZhHant: contribute to 中的 to 若引入由 contribute 選取的動詞補語，動詞須用 -ing。名詞補語，以及表示目的、附屬於名詞、捐獻內容或整個 contribute 事件的不定詞，均須排除。

ruleFamilies.name: Finite verb agrees with its syntactic subject

ruleFamilies.name: Use many, not much, with plural count nouns, including the many more construction
ruleFamilies.explanationZhHant: much 若直接限定可數複數名詞，或經由 more 形成 much more + 複數名詞，應改為 many。正確的 much fewer、副詞、代詞、疑問、不可數及詞義未確定用法均須排除。

ruleFamilies.name: Use singular hand in the contrastive marker on the other hand
ruleFamilies.explanationZhHant: on the other hands 若作句子層面的轉折語，應改為 on the other hand；實際手部方位、複合詞、標題及引文均須排除。

04 Rule Families.name: Extend GF_ALTHOUGH_NO_COORDINATING_BUT with parser-linked clause captures
04 Rule Families.explanationEn: Executable GF_ family ID for the parser matcher. It extends the approved legacy rule CONJ_ALTHOUGH_NO_COORDINATING_BUT, which is retained only in legacyRuleIdsJson. The matcher detects an although-marked subordinate clause followed by a main-clause-initial but.

04 Rule Families.name: Use a gerund after selected prepositional to in contribute to, while excluding nominal and purpose frames
04 Rule Families.explanationEn: When contribute selects a to-prepositional verbal complement, the complement is gerundial. Nominal complements and purpose infinitives attached to a noun, donation or contributing event are excluded.
04 Rule Families.explanationZhHantHK: contribute to 中的 to 若引入由 contribute 選取的動詞補語，動詞須用 -ing。名詞補語，以及表示目的、附屬於名詞、捐獻內容或整個 contribute 事件的不定詞，均須排除。

04 Rule Families.name: Extend GF_PREVENT_FROM_GERUND to active, passive and to-plus-gerund learner errors
04 Rule Families.explanationEn: Matcher extension for existing GF_PREVENT_FROM_GERUND. It captures the blocked participant as either an active object or passive subject, detects erroneous to before an infinitive or gerund, and chooses a typed repair path that inflects only when necessary. Direct-object uses and licensed British English zero-from gerunds remain protected.
04 Rule Families.explanationZhHantHK: 沿用既有 GF_PREVENT_FROM_GERUND。matcher 可把主動句受詞或被動句主語視為受阻參與者，並偵測 to + 不定詞或 to + 動名詞；只有在需要時才產生 -ing 形式。直接受詞用法及英式英語可接受的零 from 結構仍須排除。

04 Rule Families.name: Extend subject–verb agreement to finite lexical, auxiliary, passive and copular carriers
04 Rule Families.explanationEn: Matcher extension for existing GF_SUBJECT_VERB_NUMBER_AGREEMENT. It captures the syntactic subject, clause head, and actual agreement carrier: a finite lexical head or an aux, aux:pass, or cop dependent. It covers progressive, passive, perfect, do-support, contracted negation, copular predicates and difficult lexical inflections.

04 Rule Families.name: Use many, not much, with plural count nouns, including the many more construction
04 Rule Families.explanationEn: Replace much with many when it quantifies a plural count noun either directly or through comparative more. Exclude grammatical much fewer, adverbial, pronominal, interrogative, mass-noun and unresolved dual-countability uses.

04 Rule Families.name: Use singular hand in the contrastive marker on the other hand
